tensions: The framework scores NEAR 9/9 and prescribes $200; judgment says $100. Both cannot be right, and the disagreement is worth naming rather than splitting quietly. The mechanical case is strong: negative funding, 15.6% volume-to-mcap, a real AI-agent narrative, an entry at 19% of the daily range rather than a breakout chase. The discretionary case is that NEAR is up 152% in thirty days, Fear and Greed printed 78 two days ago, and total market cap is down 2.5% today - buying the month's biggest winner with every dollar of dry powder on a greed print is how good frameworks produce bad entries. Second tension: idle cash is not free. $208.69 is 10.1% of the book earning nothing in a tape where the median alt returned 14% in a week; the cost of caution is real and should be stated, not hidden behind the word discipline. Third: W is the weakest holding on every risk axis - $80M cap, $11M daily volume, a 2.1% Robinhood spread, and an unlock schedule this scan could not verify - yet it is up 11.4% and only clears the hold window tomorrow, so the rules forbid touching it today. Holding a position because the calendar says so, while knowing it is the worst thing in the book, is the price of having rules at all.

opening.text: Book $2,064 on $1,231 deposited - up 67.6%. All nine positions green, nothing over the 25% cap, not one redeploy trigger within 18% of tripping. NEAR +97.6%, LTC +40.3%, ONDO +35.6%. The correct action today is almost nothing, which is the hardest action to take.

Three items off-book. ZEC trimmed 0.12858 on Sep 25 at $1,555 - clean exit near the high, but the table still carried 0.32751. AVAX 9.0511 sits in the account with no buy order on record back to Aug 17 and no line in the tracking table: roughly $99 of book with no cost basis. And the fee tier slipped back to 0.95% taker from 0.75%, so a round trip now costs about 1.9% in explicit fees before spread.

The SUI round trip is the lesson of the week. Bought $199.94 at 20:22 ET on Sep 25, sold $193.12 at 22:53 ET. Two hours thirty-one minutes, minus $6.82, no thesis change in between - just a price wiggle and an itchy hand. SUI then posted the best seven-day return in the entire universe at +39.8%. The seven-day minimum hold is not bureaucracy; it is the rule that would have kept that $6.82 and the 40% behind it.

Regime is alt-led, not BTC-led: dominance 58.2% but Bitcoin only +3.2% over seven days against a median alt +14.0%, so dominance is falling and the rotation check does not fire. What makes it credible rather than frothy is funding - flat to negative on every holding, NEAR at -0.0076% while price is up 35%. Shorts are paying in a Greed-74 tape. That is spot demand, not leverage. Call: $100 into NEAR on the -5.6% dip, half the framework size, keeping about $109 dry.
